__comment: Grafana dashboard JSON for the wakir-persona-engine Tag-22 BackendDecision observability surface (Noa Bergstroem / SRE). Consumes Prometheus gauges produced by scripts/backend-decision-observability.py. Schema version targets Grafana 10.x (schemaVersion >= 38). Each of the five Phase-3b components (recovery, state_backing, fsm, v907_verify, bridge_diff) gets a dedicated python-vs-rust counter panel. An aggregated fallback-rate panel and a per-component latency-comparison histogram round out the picture. ADR-0061 et seq Phase-3b production-default switches (Tag-17..Tag-21).
title: Wakir Persona-Engine - Backend Decisions

panels.title: recovery — python vs rust (current window)
panels.description: Per-boot count of the 'recovery' component decisions, split python vs rust. Tag-17 (PR #168) wired the recovery switch as the first Phase-3b production-default. A sustained python skew here in a Rust-default deployment means the binary is missing or non-executable on the host — check the fallback_reason panel below.

panels.title: state_backing — python vs rust (current window)
panels.description: Per-boot count of the 'state_backing' component decisions, split python vs rust (rust splits further into rust_inmemory / rust_natskv depending on the requested storage adapter). Tag-17 (PR #168) wired this twin emit-point alongside recovery. The dual rust-flavour split is intentional — rust_natskv implies a NATS-KV-backed run while rust_inmemory implies a smoke-test or ephemeral session.

panels.title: fsm — python vs rust (current window)
panels.description: Per-boot count of the 'fsm' component decisions, split python vs rust. Tag-18 (PR #169) wired the fsm switch as the third Phase-3b production-default. The Rust pendant is the persona-engine-fsm crate (PR #137, schema-byte-parity).

panels.title: v907_verify — python vs rust (current window)
panels.description: Per-boot count of the 'v907_verify' component decisions, split python vs rust. Tag-19 (PR #171) wired the v907_verify switch. V-907 is the MOST CRITICAL of the Phase-3b switches: it is the spec §5 hash-determinism anchor — every wire-frame depends on the verifier returning a byte-identical pin across both backends. A sustained python skew is acceptable (parity-safe fallback); a sustained MIXED skew within the same deployment indicates a partial Rust rollout that needs auditing.

panels.title: bridge_diff — python vs rust (current window)
panels.description: Per-boot count of the 'bridge_diff' component decisions, split python vs rust. Tag-20 (PR #175) wired the bridge_diff switch as the fifth and most recent Phase-3b production-default. The bridge-diff component computes the cross-language diff between Python and Rust persona-engine outputs — it is itself part of the doppelbetrieb-comparison substrate and must boot stably.

panels.title: Sample Size (current window)
panels.description: Number of backend-decision records aggregated in the current sliding window. A reading < window_size means the JSONL has not yet saturated; readings AT window_size mean the gauge is steady-state.

panels.title: Aggregated Fallback Rate (cross-component, current window)
panels.description: Total fallbacks divided by total decisions across all five Phase-3b components in the current sliding window. A fallback happens when the operator requested a Rust backend but the switch had to coerce down to Python (binary_missing, binary_not_executable). Target is 0.0 in a healthy Rust-default deployment; sustained >0.05 across any 30-minute window is an Error-Budget-burn signal worth paging on.

panels.title: Per-Component Fallback Rate Over Time
panels.description: Per-component fallback-rate trend across the dashboard time range. The aggregated gauge tells you 'something is fallback-ing'; this panel tells you WHICH component. A single component spiking while the others stay green usually means a missed binary install or a path-pinning regression on the latest Rust release.

panels.title: Decision-Resolution Latency p50/p95/p99 per Component
panels.description: Nearest-rank percentile of the BackendDecision resolution-latency (microseconds) per Phase-3b component in the current sliding window. The decision step is the substrate hot-path on the engine-boot critical path: a healthy switch resolves in <50us p99 (env-var read + file-stat). Sustained p99 outside the 100us envelope on any single component is an Error-Budget-burn signal worth investigating (often: a flaky NFS-mounted bin_path or a stat-cache invalidation storm).

panels.title: Last Aggregator Scrape (unix seconds)
panels.description: POSIX-epoch timestamp at which the backend-decision aggregator last wrote the textfile. A value that stops advancing means the systemd-timer wrapper has stalled and the dashboard is showing stale data.

panels.title: Per-Component Avg Decision Latency (us, current window)
panels.description: Arithmetic mean decision-resolution latency per component. Useful as a single-glance per-component overview; the percentile panel above is the actionable diagnosis surface.
